To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FOXO3A gene variation is associated with insulin sensitivity in twins.

1) FOXO3A mRNA and protein expression in human skeletal muscle was increased in type 2 diabetic individuals compared with nondiabetic controls; 2) FOXO3G mRNA and protein expression was associated with insulin resistance in nondiabetic twins; and 3) the FOXO3A G-allele associates, independently of insulin resistance, with increased skeletal muscle-FOXA3 mRNA expression and improved peripheral and hepatal insulin sensitivity in nondiabetic individuals.
FOXO3A is associated with insulin sensitivity in human twins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the transcription factor FOXO3A in human insulin sensitivity.
the effects of FOXO3A gene variation on the development of type 2 diabetes and its related phenotypes, and the mechanisms by which FOXO3A exerts its effect.
the effects of FOXO3A polymorphisms on the development of type 2 diabetes and the associated metabolic phenotypes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FOXO3A G allele associates with improved peripheral (muscle and adipose tissue) and hepatic insulin action.
the G-allele of the rs2802292 polymorphism is not associated with the risk of type 2 diabetes.
there is no evidence to suggest that there is an association between the rs2802292 polymorphism in the FOXO3A gene and type 2 diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the G-allele of rs2802292 in FOXO3A is associated with increased insulin sensitivity and improved glucose homeostasis.

the rs2802292 polymorphism of the FOXO3A gene is associated with increased peripheral insulin sensitivity and decreased hepatic insulin sensitivity, and this association is mediated via increased skeletal muscle- FOXO3A mRNA levels.
the rs2802292 polymorphism in the FOXO3A gene is associated with insulin sensitivity in twins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a genetic variant in the FOXO3A gene that is associated with better glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity in humans.
the FOXO3A gene is a promising target for future therapeutic interventions to improve insulin sensitivity and prevent the onset of T2D.
the FOXO3A gene may contribute to the genetic variation in insulin sensitivity and that the G-allele at the rs2802292 SNP may be associated with increased insulin sensitivity in skeletal muscle.
